description: Five oscillators that pull each other into and out of step, summed into one output

params.text: Sets that oscillator's frequency as a multiple of the played note, 0 to 10, rounded to a seven hundred and twentieth
Sets that oscillator's wave, 0 to 10, from a sine at the bottom through progressively richer harmonic spectra
Sets how loudly that oscillator sounds and how strongly it pulls on the others, 0 to 2
Sets how hard the five oscillators pull on each other, -0.2 to 0.2; negative settings push them apart instead
Blends the shape of the pull between a single hump at 0 and a double one at 1, which changes whether the oscillators lock in step or in opposition
Sets how much the FM jack bends the pitch, 0 to 1

inputs.text: Adds to that oscillator's frequency ratio knob, one unit per volt
Adds to that oscillator's wave knob, one unit per volt
Adds to the coupling strength knob, one unit per volt
Adds to the coupling type knob, one unit per volt
Bends the pitch of all five oscillators through the FM knob
Adds to the gain knob, one unit per volt
Sets the note all five oscillators are tuned from, a volt per octave about C4

outputs.text: Carries the sum of the five oscillators, clipped at 5V

notes: the charm knobs have no jack of their own: they are the only controls on this module that cannot be modulated
with the coupling strength at zero the five oscillators run independently and the output is a plain additive mix; raise it and they start to fall into step
the knobs and jacks other than pitch are read once every hundred and twenty samples, so they respond a little more slowly than audio rate
